question: to the Commission Valentina Palmisano (The Left), Pasquale Tridico (The Left), Gaetano Pedulla' (The Left), Dario Tamburrano (The Left), Danilo Della Valle (The Left), Carolina Morace (The Left), Mario Furore (The Left) Subject:

The Grottaglie plant of Leonardo S.p.A. – of key importance to the Boeing 787 – is going through a period of considerable industrial uncertainty. In the wake of the wage support programme in 2024, concerns remain about the future of the site, threatened by the possible hiving-off of the aerostructures division and the entry of foreign investors, such as the Saudi Arabian PIF fund1. The trade unions are decrying the lack of an industrial plan and are concerned about the loss of skills. Civil aviation provides long-term stable employment. Conversion to military aviation, which is characterised by much lower production rates, would fail to fill the facilities designed for the high rates in civilian aviation, leading to under-utilisation and drastic job cuts. The site employs around 1 300 direct workers for the 787, supporting a local supply chain that would be at risk of collapse2. In the light of Directive 2002/14/EC, Article 27 of the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights, Directive (EU) 2019/1023 and Regulation (EU) 2019/452: 1.
Does the Commission believe that the arrangements for the potential divestment of the aerostructures division comply with EU obligations to inform and consult employees?

What tools will it use to assess the impact of these operations on employment and safeguard strategic skills in the EU’s aerospace sector, thus avoiding the loss of vital civil know-how for these areas?

answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.5.2026) Companies must respect the body of EU law, which includes Directive 2002/14 on a general framework on information and consultation of employees1. It lays down minimum requirements for the protection of workers by providing for information and consultation of workers’ representatives on a company’s activities, economic status, and changes to employment. Italy has transposed the Directive into national law2, and it is for the competent national authorities to ensure that an individual employer complies with national rules transposing it, having regard to the specific circumstances of each case. The Commission has launched work3 on an EU Aviation and Aeronautics Strategy, to set out a comprehensive framework to strengthen Europe’s aviation and aeronautical sectors at a time of heightened uncertainty. It will also strengthen the aviation sector’s capacity to respond to crises and security challenges. As for the Aerospace sector, the transition pathway4 initiative identified 53 priority actions to support the twin transitions and the long-term resilience and competitiveness of the aerospace ecosystem. As regards specifically skills, the Commission is working on the implementation of the Union of skills5, a comprehensive strategy to improve high quality education, training, and lifelong learning. The Union of skills includes a series of initiatives to step up skills intelligence and governance at EU level, including the setting up of a European Skills Intelligence Observatory providing strategic data and foresight regarding skills. Such Observatory will also inform the work of the future European Skills High-Level Board6, a newly established group which will provide comprehensive insights on skills to the EU policy makers.
1 Directive 2002/14/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 March 2002 establishing a general

framework for informing and consulting employees in the European Community, OJ L 80, 23.3.2002, p. 29–34. 2 Legislative Decree of 6 February 2007, No 25. 3 Citizens, businesses, and stakeholders were invited to share their feedback at https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/17372-EU-aviation-strategy_en 4 https://defence-industry-space.ec.europa.eu/newsroom/transition-pathway_en . 5 https://commission.europa.eu/topics/competitiveness/union-skills_en. 6 https://employment-social-affairs.ec.europa.eu/policies-and-activities/skills-and-qualifications/unionskills/european-skills-high-level-board_en.
